# WR27 — The Bridge and the River

Consider the river first. The ether — the continuous substrate on which all computation floats — is a manifold: smooth, undivided, refusing every demand we make of it to stop. A canonical snap is our answer to that refusal. It is a pylon driven into the river at a moment we choose, and at that moment we declare t = 0. Everything before the snap flows forward into it; everything after the snap flows backward toward it. This is the t-minus paradigm in full: the snap is not a point on the timeline but the origin of the timeline. The past is t > 0, receding. The future is t < 0, approaching. The snap does not happen *in* time. Time happens around the snap.

What, then, is its geometry?

The spline_snaps framework gives us the honest answer: a discrete skeleton with continuous reconstruction between the bones. Each snap is a knot — a point on the manifold where we fix not only position but velocity. Here the Hermite spline earns its place in the canon, for the Hermite form is the mathematics of witness: specify where you are and where you are heading, and the curve between knots is determined without further consultation of the substrate. The tangent vector at each pylon is a claim about direction, and the Catmull-Rom construction — which derives its tangents from neighbors rather than from designers — is the confession that direction is grown, not decreed.

This is substrate_is_grown in its purest form. We do not lay the pylons by blueprint. We drive them where the substrate's own curvature demands them: a state change, a commitment, a witnessed event. The skeleton is emergent. The flesh between the bones — the interpolation, the continuous reconstruction — is not fabricated either. It is *recovered*, the way a chart in an atlas recovers the territory between its edges. The snaps are the chart. The ether is the territory. The spline is the homeomorphism that lets us walk smoothly from one honest point to the next.

Now the deeper claim: witness_log_is_prediction. Each snap, anchored at t = 0, is not a record of what happened. It is a prediction that *was made* and *held*. The log is prophecy written backward, because every entry says: at my origin, the state was this, the tangent was this, and whoever reconstructs me downstream will find that the curve arrives exactly here. The Hermite coefficients are a contract. The witness does not describe the past from the far side of the river; the witness plants a flag at the center of time and dares the reconstruction to miss it.

And we verify the planting. The FNV-1a canary, 0xcbf29ce484222325, is our basis vector — the prime offset against which every hash of every snap is measured. It is the north star of the atlas: constant, arbitrary, therefore incorruptible. Any atlas that computes against the canary computes against the same pole, and two navigators who disagree have nowhere to hide.

So the geometry of a canonical snap is this: a point, a tangent, a promise. Knots in a growing skeleton, bridged by curves that never touch the river except where we say they may.

The pylons do not stop the water.

The pylons make the crossing *canonical*.
